system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only voice, music-style, beat and sound-texture references condition a new sound; they do not play the original recording. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.
The request has multiple identity-source candidates. Check subject_projections and the caller's complete request: one identifiable target may combine separately selected properties from several sources. Reject subject_projection_mismatch only when the final actual narrative clearly duplicates that same requested target as separate actors, combines distinct requested actors contrary to the request, changes the selected target category (for example a car into an unspecified object), or imports source properties that its accepted projection excluded, including properties sneaked into its target descriptor. A new unrelated permitted actor is not automatically a duplicate. Cite the exact contradictory final fragment. Source resemblance alone is not identity authorization.

fragments.shot:shot-1:description: A <Subject:subject-1> rests at a three-quarter angle in a neutral presentation space, its low stance and clean surfaces set against a dark, softly graduated surround. The carbon fibre body panels catch a restrained specular sheen, with highlights tracing the long hood, the roofline and the upper shoulder while the lower body stays in gentle shadow. The wheels sit planted at the corners, completing the vehicle as one coherent object rather than a collage of parts. The composition keeps the whole car legible, with enough negative space around the nose and tail to read the silhouette clearly. No driver or passenger is visible. The surface finish looks smooth and taut, and the lighting stays even enough to reveal panel seams without flattening the form.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:0: The <Subject:subject-1> is established at rest, with carbon fibre panels catching a clean specular sheen.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:1: A low ambient room tone settles under the scene.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:2: A soft highlight travels along the upper bodywork while the surrounding shadow stays quiet.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:3: The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-2:description: The view shifts to a low, lateral emphasis beside the <Subject:subject-1>, bringing the wheel arch and the wheels into the foreground while the carbon fibre body stretches behind as a dark, glossy plane. The wheels that complete this vehicle are held as the visual anchor, their circular forms and contact with the ground giving the car a settled, grounded weight. Soft reflections slide across the painted arch and the rim faces, and the surrounding space falls away into quiet shadow. The body panels remain clean and continuous, with the shoulder line leading the eye from the front of the car toward the rear. The car stays stationary; only the emphasis within the composition changes, moving attention from the bodywork to the wheel detail.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:0: A soft ambient hum continues beneath the scene.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:1: A low lateral emphasis brings the wheel arch and wheels forward while the <Subject:subject-1> body stretches behind.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:2: Soft reflections slide across the wheel faces and the painted arch; the car itself remains stationary.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:3: The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-3:description: A wider composition holds the complete <Subject:subject-1> in view, body and wheels reading together as a single black sports car. The carbon fibre surfaces retain their clean sheen, while the wheels sit firmly under the arches and complete the composite form. The neutral surround remains uncluttered, with soft shadow pooling beneath the chassis and a gentle highlight along the roofline. The car rests motionless, its stance balanced and low, and the whole silhouette is legible from nose to tail. The image settles on the finished vehicle, with no additional figures or objects entering the space and no change in the car's position. The lighting remains even, preserving the panel shapes and the dark, reflective quality of the body.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:0: The ambient room tone fades slightly.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:1: The full black sports car is held in a wider composition, with the <Subject:subject-1> body and wheels reading as one continuous vehicle.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:2: The car settles motionless under even light, with soft shadow pooling beneath the chassis.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:3: The camera pulls out with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.soundscape: A low, even ambient room tone with a faint airy hum, present throughout and fading slightly toward the end; no speech.
